Dataset: 1993 sketch, company leachate/COD records, four candidate locations around the eastern yard. Baseline: 1993 conceptual model and single in-house COD value. Researcher compares two flow-direction scenarios with a simple MODFLOW/MT3DMS model; company supplies site records. Measure: head residuals, COD gradient, inferred flow direction. Go/no-go: proceed to permanent siting only if split-sample COD confirms the 3,400 mg/L order of magnitude, at least two locations show a consistent COD gradient, and head residuals are <0.5 m; otherwise revise the model and re-site. Overall gate: four wells installed and containment/treatment proposal accepted by the inspectorate by late June 2024.

Proposed success criteria: flow direction identified from at least two independent head measurements; COD gradient detected in at least two wells; final network reproduces observed heads within 0.5 m; draft proposal addresses all inspectorate-required parameters. These are negotiation targets, not guaranteed outcomes.

Proposed containment/treatment screening: compare at least two options, such as hydraulic containment by pumping and a low-permeability surface barrier, against measured COD and site conditions; company supplies cost and operational constraints; researcher supplies design basis and regulator-facing rationale.

content.markdown:
# Leachate plume characterisation and monitoring-well design for Zelena Petlja's temporary storage yard

## Verified facts
- Leachate is seeping toward the site boundary; COD is 3,400 mg/L, well above the formal-response threshold; the Subotica Environmental Inspectorate ordered four groundwater monitoring wells within 120 days and a remediation proposal by late June 2024. [F1]
- Baseline data are almost absent: only a 1993 hydrogeological sketch exists, and contamination extent and seasonal groundwater-flow direction are unknown. [F2]
- The output must be a leachate containment and treatment proposal acceptable to the inspectorate, not only monitoring. [F3]
- The company has no dedicated research budget and only a basic wet-chemistry bench; its COD value came from its in-house bench. [F4]
- The researcher's consulting experience includes advising a provincial water utility on site characterisation methodology and monitoring network design. [F5]
- He has field experience with 18 multi-level piezometers at three riverbank transects at a bank-filtration site, and monitoring-network installation at two BF sites and two recharge transects. [F6]
- His transport evidence is a calibrated groundwater-flow and MT3DMS particle-tracking numerical study; particle tracking indicated median travel times of 18–42 days at a production well field. [F7]
- He is open to joint projects and contract research on site-specific hydrogeological assessment, prefers field measurement, and has industrial-PhD co-supervision capacity starting autumn 2026. [F8]

## Our inference
- The documented field sites are riverbank bank-filtration, agricultural recharge transects and canals; this suggests the monitoring and modelling methods must be tested for a waste-yard leachate setting rather than assumed transferable.
- His transport modelling is particle tracking at a well field, not reactive leachate transport; predicting COD behaviour in the subsurface is therefore an unproven extension for this site.
- The proposal is conditional: his availability in the 120-day window is not confirmed, and the industrial-PhD route starting autumn 2026 cannot meet a late-June 2024 deadline, so a joint project is the only feasible format if he is available.

## Proposed next steps
- Proposed first experiment: reconnaissance and siting test before drilling the four ordered wells. Dataset: 1993 sketch, company leachate/COD records, four candidate locations around the eastern yard. Baseline: 1993 conceptual model and single in-house COD value. Change: install temporary piezometers/soil borings (company arranges access and staff; researcher designs locations and sampling), measure water level, COD, EC and chloride in leachate and shallow groundwater, and take a split sample for independent COD confirmation. Researcher compares two flow-direction scenarios with a simple MODFLOW/MT3DMS model; company supplies site records. Measure: head residuals, COD gradient, inferred flow direction. Go/no-go: proceed to permanent siting only if split-sample COD confirms the 3,400 mg/L order of magnitude, at least two locations show a consistent COD gradient, and head residuals are <0.5 m; otherwise revise the model and re-site. Overall gate: four wells installed and containment/treatment proposal accepted by the inspectorate by late June 2024.
- Proposed timeline: weeks 1–2 desk review and sampling plan; weeks 3–4 access, permits and contractor quotes; weeks 5–8 reconnaissance and temporary piezometers; weeks 9–12 final siting, drilling and sampling; weeks 13–16 modelling and draft proposal before late June 2024.
- Proposed success criteria: flow direction identified from at least two independent head measurements; COD gradient detected in at least two wells; final network reproduces observed heads within 0.5 m; draft proposal addresses all inspectorate-required parameters. These are negotiation targets, not guaranteed outcomes.
- Proposed containment/treatment screening: compare at least two options, such as hydraulic containment by pumping and a low-permeability surface barrier, against measured COD and site conditions; company supplies cost and operational constraints; researcher supplies design basis and regulator-facing rationale.

## Open questions
- Can the researcher confirm availability to start field work within the 120-day window (spring 2024) and agree to a joint project rather than an industrial PhD?
- Who will fund and carry out drilling, well installation and any accredited laboratory analyses, and which drilling permits are required?
- What site information exists beyond the 1993 sketch: depth to water table, liner details, existing boreholes, and nearby production or monitoring wells?
- Which parameters and analytical standards will the inspectorate require, and is an accredited laboratory available for confirmatory COD and leachate analyses?
- What waste types and volumes were stored in the yard over twelve years, and were hazardous items present that would change leachate composition?
